components.note: 灬 (fire) — 热 relates directly to heat
执 (zhí) gives a loose sound connection to 热's reading rè
犭 (dog/animal) — 狗 names an animal, the dog.
句 (jù) gives a sound distantly related to gǒu, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他午饭只吃了一根热狗。
example.pinyin: Tā wǔfàn zhǐ chīle yī gēn règǒu.
example.english: He only ate a hot dog for lunch.
example.fact: The hot dog's name may come from German immigrant vendors in 19th-century America who sold sausages from carts nicknamed "dog wagons," since sausage meat was jokingly rumored to contain dog meat. A popular but unverified story credits a 1901 New York cartoonist with popularizing the term because he couldn't spell "dachshund."

components.note: 马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.
The character traces the head and shaft of a simple nail, a shape later borrowed for other meanings.

example.hanzi: 马丁在会议上提出了一个新方案。
example.pinyin: Mǎdīng zài huìyì shàng tíchūle yī gè xīn fāng'àn.
example.english: Martin proposed a new plan at the meeting.
example.fact: Martin is the root of the word "martinet," a strict disciplinarian, named after Jean Martinet, a 17th-century French drill instructor whose rigid training methods became legendary in the army of Louis XIV. The word entered English within decades of his death in 1672.

components.note: A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 这部片子讲的是一个探险家的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù piānzi jiǎng de shì yī gè tànxiǎnjiā de gùshì.
example.english: This film tells the story of an explorer.
example.fact: Early film reels were made of nitrate stock so flammable that projectionists worked in fireproof booths, since the material could ignite from the heat of the projector lamp alone and, once burning, released its own oxygen and kept burning even underwater. Studios didn't fully switch to safer acetate "safety film" until the 1950s.

components.note: 木 (tree) forms the base.
一 marks the very top of the tree, giving 末 its meaning 'end, tip, final.'
日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.

example.hanzi: 这部电影描绘了世界末日的景象。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng miáohuìle shìjiè mòrì de jǐngxiàng.
example.english: This movie depicts a vision of the world's doomsday.
example.fact: The Doomsday Clock, maintained by the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists since 1947, is a symbolic countdown to global catastrophe measured in minutes and seconds to midnight. In January 2023 the clock was moved to 90 seconds to midnight, its closest setting ever, citing the war in Ukraine and nuclear risk.

components.note: Rice/grain — sugar was traditionally made from grains or cane.
Gives the sound táng, matching the character's reading.
田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'

example.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢在万圣节收集糖果。
example.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan zài Wànshèngjié shōují tángguǒ.
example.english: Children love collecting candy on Halloween.
example.fact: The world's oldest known candy, found in an Egyptian tomb, was made from honey mixed with fruits and nuts, since refined sugar did not reach the Mediterranean world until centuries later. Sugarcane itself was first domesticated in New Guinea around 8,000 years ago before spreading to India and beyond.

components.note: 目 depicts an eye turned on its side, with the outline and pupil visible — later straightened into today's rectangular shape.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'

者's ancient form combined a plant growing from the ground with a mouth-like element beneath it; the original picture is debated, but the character was borrowed for its sound to serve as a grammatical suffix meaning 'the one who' or 'the thing that,' its main modern function.

example.hanzi: 警方正在寻找案件的目击者。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài xúnzhǎo ànjiàn de mùjīzhě.
example.english: The police are looking for witnesses to the case.
example.fact: Cognitive psychologists have repeatedly shown that eyewitness memory is far less reliable than juries tend to assume, since stress, the presence of a weapon, and even the wording of a later question can distort a memory after the fact. DNA-exoneration studies of wrongful convictions in the United States found mistaken eyewitness identification was a contributing factor in a majority of the cases reviewed.

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 雨后地面变得又湿又滑。
example.pinyin: Yǔ hòu dìmiàn biàn de yòu shī yòu huá.
example.english: After the rain, the ground became wet and slippery.
example.fact: Earth's land surface makes up only about 29% of the planet, with the rest covered by ocean, yet nearly all of human agriculture and infrastructure depends on that thin sliver of ground. Antarctica's ice sheet alone, if it melted, would raise global sea level by roughly 58 meters.

meanings: also pr. [dai1 hui3 r5] or [dai1 hui5 r5]

components.note: 彳 (a road/step) — someone arriving on the road
寺 (a court/hall) — the destination where the visitor is welcomed
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.

example.hanzi: 你先坐一下,我待会儿就回来。
example.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zuò yīxià, wǒ dāihuìr jiù huílái.
example.english: Sit down for a moment; I'll be back shortly.
example.fact: The perception that time passes differently under stress or boredom is well documented: psychologists have found that people asked to estimate elapsed time during a frightening event, such as a fall, consistently overestimate the duration afterward, even though their real-time judgment during the event is accurate. This gap is attributed to how densely the brain encodes memories during high-adrenaline moments.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.hanzi: 医生提醒他不要过度饮酒。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng tíxǐng tā bùyào guòdù yǐnjiǔ.
example.english: The doctor reminded him not to drink excessively.
example.fact: The human liver can regenerate itself even after up to 70% of its tissue is removed or damaged, restoring most of its original mass within weeks. This remarkable capacity is also why liver transplants can come from living donors, who each regrow a functional liver from the portion they keep.

components.note: 声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.
禾 (grain) — 称 originally described weighing grain on a scale, which extended to its meanings 'to weigh' and 'to call, to be named.'
尔 replaces the traditional phonetic component 爯 in the simplified form; its reading ěr sits only loosely close to chēng today, the two having drifted apart over centuries of sound change.

example.hanzi: 该公司声称其产品完全无害。
example.pinyin: Gāi gōngsī shēngchēng qí chǎnpǐn wánquán wúhài.
example.english: The company claims its products are completely harmless.
example.fact: In 1938, tobacco companies began running ads in which doctors claimed cigarettes were harmless or even good for the throat, a marketing tactic historians now cite as an early case study in corporate disinformation. Internal industry memos, unsealed decades later during litigation, showed executives privately knew otherwise as far back as the 1950s.

components.note: A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'
玨 (two connected jade pieces, standing in for strings) shows 瑟 relates to a stringed instrument.
必 (bì) gives a sound distantly related to sè, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 亚瑟王的传说流传了上千年。
example.pinyin: Yàsè wáng de chuánshuō liúchuánle shàng qiān nián.
example.english: The legend of King Arthur has been passed down for over a thousand years.
example.fact: Historians still debate whether King Arthur was based on a real person, since no contemporary record from the 5th or 6th century mentions him; the earliest surviving references appear only centuries later, in Welsh chronicles written around 830 AD. Most scholars now treat Arthur as a composite folk hero rather than a single historical figure.

meanings: variant of 諮詢|咨询[zi1 xun2]

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咨 relates to speaking, asking for advice.
次 (cì) gives a sound only distantly related to zī today, having drifted apart over time.
讠 (speech) shows 询 relates to asking or speaking.
旬 (xún) gives the exact sound of 询.

example.hanzi: 她去医院咨询了营养师的建议。
example.pinyin: Tā qù yīyuàn zīxúnle yíngyǎngshī de jiànyì.
example.english: She went to the hospital to consult a nutritionist for advice.
example.fact: The modern management-consulting industry traces back to the early 20th century and firms like McKinsey & Company, founded in 1926, which grew out of the scientific-management movement pioneered by Frederick Taylor. That movement itself began not in offices but on factory floors, where Taylor timed workers with a stopwatch to optimize steel-mill efficiency.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
广 depicts a roofed building or shelter.
廷 depicts an open court or hall — together with the shelter above, giving 庭 its meaning 'courtyard, hall.'

example.hanzi: 证人明天必须出庭作证。
example.pinyin: Zhèngrén míngtiān bìxū chūtíng zuòzhèng.
example.english: The witness must appear in court tomorrow to testify.
example.fact: The oldest surviving law code requiring courtroom-style testimony, the Code of Ur-Nammu from ancient Sumer around 2100 BC, already specified procedures for witnesses and evidence nearly a thousand years before Hammurabi's more famous code. Clay tablets recording actual Mesopotamian trial proceedings have survived to this day in museum archives.

components.note: 勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'
囗 (an enclosure) — 围 relates to surrounding or encircling something
韦 (wéi) gives the sound — 围 is also pronounced wéi, an exact match

example.hanzi: 警察迅速包围了那栋大楼。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá xùnsù bāowéile nà dòng dàlóu.
example.english: The police quickly surrounded that building.
example.fact: Wolves hunting in packs often encircle prey from multiple directions, a coordinated strategy that lets a group half the size of a moose or elk bring it down through exhaustion rather than raw strength. Biologists studying Yellowstone wolf packs have documented these encirclement tactics changing in real time based on terrain and the number of hunters available.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
A pictograph of an altar or offering table used in ancestor worship — presenting offerings extended to 示's meaning 'to show, display, indicate.'

example.hanzi: 老师在黑板上写了一个提示。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài hēibǎn shàng xiěle yī gè tíshì.
example.english: The teacher wrote a hint on the blackboard.
example.fact: Search engines and video games alike rely on a psychological principle called the "hint gradient," where a subtle nudge is more effective at prompting problem-solving than either total silence or an outright answer. Research on hint design shows that the most useful hints redirect attention rather than reveal the solution outright, preserving the sense of discovery.

components.note: 米 (grain/rice) — 糊 originally referred to a paste made from rice or grain.
胡 (hú) gives the sound — an exact match with 糊.
Water — early sense linked to a river name, later extended to smearing liquid.
Gives the sound yú, related to tú but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他喝多了酒,脑子有点糊涂。
example.pinyin: Tā hē duō le jiǔ, nǎozi yǒudiǎn hútu.
example.english: He drank too much and his mind was a bit muddled.
example.fact: Alcohol impairs the hippocampus, the brain region responsible for forming new long-term memories, well before it noticeably affects motor coordination, which is why a person can appear to function normally while later having no memory of the events at all. This gap between apparent lucidity and memory formation is what researchers call an alcohol-induced "blackout."

components.note: 火 (fire) shows 燃 relates directly to burning.
然 (rán) gives the exact sound of 燃.
火 (fire) — 烧 describes burning or cooking with fire.
尧 (yáo) gives a rhyme close to shāo, with a different initial.

example.hanzi: 森林大火燃烧了整整三天。
example.pinyin: Sēnlín dàhuǒ ránshāole zhěngzhěng sān tiān.
example.english: The forest fire burned for three whole days.
example.fact: Some wildfires burn so intensely that they generate their own weather, producing towering pyrocumulonimbus clouds that can trigger lightning strikes and start entirely new fires far from the original blaze. The 2019-2020 Australian bushfire season produced dozens of these fire-generated thunderstorms in a single fire season.

components.note: 豕 (boar) — 豪 originally described a fierce, bristling boar-like porcupine, extending to 'heroic, grand.'
高 (gāo) shares the rhyme -ao with háo, though the initial has drifted from g- to h- over time.
十 (ten, suggesting abundance) — relates to 华's meaning 'flowery, splendid,' an abundance of blossoms.
化 (huà) gives a sound hint — 华 is pronounced huá, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这家酒店的大堂十分豪华。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de dàtáng shífēn háohuá.
example.english: This hotel's lobby is extremely luxurious.
example.fact: The Titanic's most luxurious first-class suites came with their own private promenade decks and cost the equivalent of over $100,000 in today's money for a one-way Atlantic crossing. Ironically, the ship's design prioritized opulent interiors over lifeboat capacity, which carried only about half the passengers and crew aboard.

components.note: 龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.hanzi: 第一次世界大战中,毒气造成了大量伤亡。
example.pinyin: Dì yī cì shìjiè dàzhàn zhōng, dúqì zàochéngle dàliàng shāngwáng.
example.english: During World War I, poison gas caused massive casualties.
example.fact: Chlorine gas, first used as a weapon by German forces at the Second Battle of Ypres in 1915, was so widely condemned afterward that the 1925 Geneva Protocol banned chemical weapons in warfare, a ban still in force today. Ironically, the same chemist who helped develop it, Fritz Haber, had earlier won acclaim for inventing a process to synthesize ammonia fertilizer that still feeds a large share of the world's population.

components.note: Hand — a fist is a closed hand.
Gives a sound distantly related to quán, having drifted apart over time.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'

example.hanzi: 他从小就开始练习拳击。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù kāishǐ liànxí quánjī.
example.english: He started practicing boxing from a young age.
example.fact: Boxing appears among the events of the ancient Olympic Games as early as 688 BC, with competitors wrapping their hands in leather straps called himantes rather than wearing padded gloves. Modern padded boxing gloves weren't introduced until the 19th century, under rules named after the Marquess of Queensberry.

components.note: A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'

当 is the simplified form of 當, which combined 田 (a field) beneath 尚 (a hall, suggesting something raised and facing outward) — one field matching or corresponding to another gave 当 its meaning 'to correspond to, to serve as, appropriate.'

example.hanzi: 亚当是圣经故事里的第一个人。
example.pinyin: Yàdāng shì Shèngjīng gùshì lǐ de dì yī gè rén.
example.english: Adam is the first man in the Bible's story.
example.fact: The name Adam is closely related to the Hebrew word "adamah," meaning "ground" or "soil," reflecting the Genesis account that the first man was formed from earth. Ancient Near Eastern creation myths from Mesopotamia, some predating Genesis by centuries, contain similar motifs of humans molded from clay by a deity.

components.note: 彡 (hair/decorative strokes) — 修 relates to grooming, decorating, or improving something
攸 (yōu) gives a sound close to 修's reading xiū, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.

example.hanzi: 那位修女在孤儿院工作了三十年。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi xiūnǚ zài gū'éryuàn gōngzuòle sānshí nián.
example.english: That nun worked at the orphanage for thirty years.
example.fact: Saint Teresa of Ávila, a 16th-century Spanish nun, reformed the Carmelite order and wrote mystical texts still studied today, and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1970 — one of the first women ever given that title. Convents in medieval Europe were also among the few institutions where women could receive a formal education and hold positions of real administrative authority.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 混 originally described muddy, mixed water.
昆 (kūn) gives a sound distantly related to hùn, having drifted apart over time.
合 pictures a lid (亼) closing down over a container's opening (口) below it — two parts fitting together perfectly, the source of 合's meaning 'to combine, to close, to agree.'

example.hanzi: 把这两种颜料混合就能得到紫色。
example.pinyin: Bǎ zhè liǎng zhǒng yánliào hùnhé jiù néng dédào zǐsè.
example.english: Mix these two pigments together and you'll get purple.
example.fact: Isaac Newton demonstrated in the 1660s that white light is not pure but a mixture of all visible colors, by passing sunlight through a prism to split it into a spectrum and then recombining the colors with a second prism to restore white light. This experiment overturned the prevailing belief that prisms themselves created color.

components.note: 爪 and 彐 (two hands, reaching from opposite sides) — a simplified form of 爭, grabbing for the same thing.
亅 (the object) — what the two hands are struggling over, giving 争 its meaning 'to contend, compete, fight for.'
口 (mouth) — arguing is done vocally.
少 (shǎo) gives a sound fairly close to chǎo, sharing the rhyme.

example.hanzi: 邻居之间因为噪音发生了争吵。
example.pinyin: Línjū zhījiān yīnwèi zàoyīn fāshēngle zhēngchǎo.
example.english: The neighbors got into a quarrel because of the noise.
example.fact: Behavioral researchers studying married couples have found that the ratio of positive to negative interactions during a disagreement predicts divorce with striking accuracy; couples averaging fewer than five positive exchanges for every negative one were far more likely to separate within years. This finding, from long-running observational studies at the University of Washington, is now widely cited in couples therapy.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 轻 originally described a light, nimble cart, extended to 'light (weight), gentle.'
工 (gōng) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from qīng.

易's oldest form has been read as a picture of a lizard or chameleon, an animal noted for changing its skin color — the likely origin of 易's meaning 'to change,' which later broadened to 'easy, simple.'

example.hanzi: 这个问题不能轻易下结论。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí bùnéng qīngyì xià jiélùn.
example.english: This problem shouldn't be concluded too hastily.
example.fact: Confirmation bias — the tendency to accept evidence that fits what we already believe without much scrutiny — was first named and studied systematically by psychologist Peter Wason in the 1960s through a simple rule-guessing experiment. His subjects overwhelmingly sought only confirming examples, rarely testing whether their hypothesis could be wrong.

components.note: 山 (mountain) surrounds the character, setting the scene.
幺 (small, doubled here) shows tiny hidden niches within the mountainside, giving 幽 its meaning 'secluded, hidden, dark.'
黑 (black/dark) pictures nightfall.
犬 (dog) pictures a dog keeping silent watch in the dark, giving 默 its meaning 'silent, still.'

example.hanzi: 他的幽默总能让大家开心起来。
example.pinyin: Tā de yōumò zǒngnéng ràng dàjiā kāixīn qǐlái.
example.english: His humor always manages to cheer everyone up.
example.fact: Laughter triggers the release of endorphins in the brain and can measurably raise a person's pain tolerance, a phenomenon researchers at Oxford confirmed by testing subjects' pain thresholds immediately after they watched comedy clips versus neutral videos. The effect appears tied to genuine social laughter rather than merely feeling amused.

components.note: 日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
知 (to know) forms the upper part of the character.
日 (sun, clarity) — knowledge seen as clearly as the sun gave 智 its meaning 'wisdom.'

example.hanzi: 做出这个明智的决定并不容易。
example.pinyin: Zuò chū zhège míngzhì de juédìng bìng bù róngyì.
example.english: Making this wise decision wasn't easy.
example.fact: The field of behavioral economics, pioneered by Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky in the 1970s, showed that human decision-making systematically deviates from purely rational models through predictable cognitive shortcuts and biases. Kahneman's later book on the subject won him a Nobel Prize in Economics in 2002, despite his having no formal training in economics at all.

components.note: 土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.

example.hanzi: 吃完晚饭我们去公园走走吧。
example.pinyin: Chī wán wǎnfàn wǒmen qù gōngyuán zǒuzǒu ba.
example.english: After dinner, let's go take a walk in the park.
example.fact: A large long-term study following thousands of adults found that walking briskly for just 11 minutes a day was associated with a meaningfully lower risk of early death and cardiovascular disease. Researchers noted the benefit curve was steepest at the very start, meaning even small amounts of walking mattered disproportionately.

components.note: 后 originally pictured a ruler issuing a command with an open mouth, giving its old meaning 'queen, empress.' Its modern sense 'behind, after' comes from an unrelated character, 後, whose meaning merged into this same simplified form.
辶 (to walk) — 退 relates to moving backward or away
艮 (gèn) gives a sound distantly related to 退's reading tuì, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 看到蛇,他吓得连忙后退了几步。
example.pinyin: Kàndào shé, tā xià de liánmáng hòutuìle jǐ bù.
example.english: Seeing the snake, he was so startled he quickly stepped back.
example.fact: The reflex that makes people jump backward from a sudden threat is controlled by a rapid, low-level pathway through the brain's amygdala that can trigger a defensive response in a fraction of a second, well before the visual cortex has fully identified what's being seen. This is why people often flinch from something later found to be harmless.

components.note: 囗 depicts an enclosure or fence.
木 (tree) — a tree hemmed in by a fence, unable to grow freely, gave 困 its meaning 'trapped, difficult.'
心 (heart) at the bottom shows this is about a state of mind.
或 (perhaps, maybe) above conveys uncertainty, giving 惑 its meaning 'to confuse, to be puzzled.'

example.hanzi: 这道数学题让全班同学都感到困惑。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào shùxué tí ràng quán bān tóngxué dōu gǎndào kùnhuò.
example.english: This math problem left the whole class feeling confused.
example.fact: The Monty Hall probability puzzle, based on a real game-show scenario, confused so many mathematicians and statisticians when it was published in 1990 that thousands wrote in to argue the correct answer was wrong, even though it can be proven with simple probability theory. Simulations later confirmed the counterintuitive solution beyond doubt.

components.note: 弋 (a dagger-axe/weapon) — represents military force.
止 (foot/to stop) — stopping an enemy by force of arms gave 武 its meaning 'military, martial.'
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match

example.hanzi: 这些反抗军装备了简易的武装力量。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē fǎnkàngjūn zhuāngbèile jiǎnyì de wǔzhuāng lìliàng.
example.english: These rebel forces were equipped with makeshift armed forces.
example.fact: Costa Rica abolished its military entirely in 1949 following a civil war, redirecting the funds toward education and healthcare, and remains one of only a handful of countries in the world today without a standing army. It relies instead on a public security force and international agreements for its defense.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.

甲's earliest form is a square divided by a cross, thought to depict a turtle's shell or a seed's outer casing splitting open — the source of 甲's meanings 'shell, armor' and, from the cyclical order used in shell-casting divination, 'first' (the first of the ten heavenly stems).

example.hanzi: 她的指甲上涂着鲜红色的指甲油。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhǐjia shàng túzhe xiānhóngsè de zhǐjiayóu.
example.english: Her fingernails were painted a bright red.
example.fact: Fingernails grow roughly three to four times faster than toenails, and the nail on the middle finger grows fastest of all, likely because it's the longest digit and gets the most blood flow and use. Nail growth also speeds up in summer and slows in winter, tracking seasonal changes in circulation.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 透 relates to moving all the way through something.
秀 (xiù) gives a sound distantly related to tòu, having drifted apart over time.
雨 (rain) — 露 names a form of moisture related to weather.
路 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 露.

example.hanzi: 有人向记者透露了这项计划的细节。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén xiàng jìzhě tòulùle zhè xiàng jìhuà de xìjié.
example.english: Someone leaked the details of this plan to a reporter.
example.fact: The Pentagon Papers, leaked to the New York Times in 1971 by military analyst Daniel Ellsberg, revealed that the U.S. government had privately known the Vietnam War was largely unwinnable years before publicly claiming otherwise. The Supreme Court ultimately ruled in the newspaper's favor, reinforcing strong First Amendment protection against government efforts to block publication.

components.note: 斗 depicts a hand-held dipper or ladle used for measuring grain and liquids — giving 斗 its meaning 'a unit of dry measure,' and by extension, the Big Dipper constellation.
爪 and 彐 (two hands, reaching from opposite sides) — a simplified form of 爭, grabbing for the same thing.
亅 (the object) — what the two hands are struggling over, giving 争 its meaning 'to contend, compete, fight for.'

example.hanzi: 工人们为了更好的待遇进行了斗争。
example.pinyin: Gōngrénmen wèile gèng hǎo de dàiyù jìnxíngle dòuzhēng.
example.english: The workers fought for better treatment.
example.fact: The eight-hour workday, now standard across much of the world, emerged from decades of labor struggle in the 19th century, symbolized by the slogan "eight hours for work, eight hours for rest, eight hours for what we will." The 1886 Haymarket affair in Chicago, a rally connected to this movement that turned violent, is why May Day is still marked as International Workers' Day in many countries.

components.note: 录 traditionally depicted a hand-held tool used for carving or writing records — the image behind its meaning 'to record, to write down.'
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.
巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'

example.hanzi: 他家阁楼里还留着几盒旧录像带。
example.pinyin: Tā jiā gélóu lǐ hái liúzhe jǐ hé jiù lùxiàngdài.
example.english: A few old videotapes are still kept in the attic of his house.
example.fact: The format war between VHS and Betamax in the late 1970s and 1980s ended largely because VHS tapes could record longer programs, even though Betamax offered somewhat sharper picture quality. Sony, Betamax's maker, eventually conceded the format war and began producing VHS players itself in 1988.

components.note: 咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'
心 (heart) — 恩 relates to feelings of gratitude and kindness.
因 (yīn) gives the sound — an exact match with 恩.
节 is the simplified form of 節, which depicted the segmented sections of a bamboo stalk ⺮ — giving 节 its meaning 'joint, section, festival.'

example.hanzi: 每年十一月的第四个星期四是感恩节。
example.pinyin: Měinián shíyī yuè de dì sì gè xīngqísì shì Gǎn'ēnjié.
example.english: Thanksgiving falls on the fourth Thursday of November every year.
example.fact: The wishbone-snapping tradition associated with Thanksgiving dates back to the ancient Etruscans, who considered chickens sacred oracles and dried their collarbones for good luck, a custom the Romans later adopted and spread across Europe. Turkeys themselves were domesticated by Indigenous peoples in Mexico long before European contact.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 灯 names a lamp, which once gave light through a small flame.
丁 (dīng) gives a sound distantly related to dēng, having drifted apart over time.
儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.

example.hanzi: 舞台上的灯光随着音乐不断变化。
example.pinyin: Wǔtái shàng de dēngguāng suízhe yīnyuè bùduàn biànhuà.
example.english: The stage lighting kept changing along with the music.
example.fact: Modern stage lighting design traces back to the introduction of electric arc lamps in 19th-century theaters, which finally let directors control brightness precisely instead of relying on gas flames or limelight, a technique that literally burned lime to incandescence. The phrase "in the limelight" comes directly from that earlier, much more dangerous lighting method.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
目 (eye) — supervising, 督's meaning, involves watching closely.
叔 (shū) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading dū has diverged.

example.hanzi: 这座教堂供奉的是耶稣基督。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiàotáng gòngfèng de shì Yēsū Jīdū.
example.english: This church is dedicated to Jesus Christ.
example.fact: The word "Christ" comes from the Greek "Christos," meaning "the anointed one," a direct translation of the Hebrew term "Messiah." It functioned originally as a title rather than a surname, describing a ritual anointing with oil historically used to consecrate kings and priests in the ancient Near East.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn
扌 (hand) — 举 relates to lifting or raising something with the hand
舉 (jǔ) is the traditional character's own form, giving the sound directly, an exact match

example.hanzi: 今年年底将举行地方选举。
example.pinyin: Jīnnián niándǐ jiāng jǔxíng dìfāng xuǎnjǔ.
example.english: Local elections will be held at the end of this year.
example.fact: Ancient Athens selected many public officials not by election but by lottery, drawing names from a device called a kleroterion, on the theory that random selection prevented wealthy citizens from buying influence over ordinary offices. Actual competitive elections were reserved mainly for a small number of high-stakes military and financial positions.

components.note: 戌 (a halberd/weapon) — represents armed force.
女 (woman) — force used to intimidate gave 威 its meaning 'power, might, awe-inspiring.'
广 (a building with a sloped roof) — 廉's early meaning referred to the sharp, straight edge or corner of a hall's wall, extending figuratively to moral 'uprightness, incorruptibility.'
兼 (jiān) sits close in sound to lián, the two readings sharing a final vowel despite the shifted initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 威廉王子出席了这次慈善晚宴。
example.pinyin: Wēilián wángzǐ chūxíle zhè cì císhàn wǎnyàn.
example.english: Prince William attended this charity dinner.
example.fact: William the Conqueror, who invaded England in 1066, commissioned the Domesday Book in 1086 — a vast property survey of nearly every landholding in the kingdom — to assess taxes, and the original manuscript survives today in the UK's National Archives. Its nickname reflects how final and unappealable its judgments about land ownership were meant to be.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 追 relates to moving in pursuit of someone or something
㠯 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 追's reading zhuī, having drifted apart over time
木 (wood) — 查 first referred to a wooden raft, a sense today usually written with the related character 槎.
旦 (dawn, the sun rising over the horizon) sits below the wood; the character was later borrowed to write the unrelated word 'to check, to inspect,' its main modern meaning.

example.hanzi: 警方正在追查这起盗窃案的线索。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài zhuīchá zhè qǐ dàoqiè'àn de xiànsuǒ.
example.english: The police are tracking down leads on this theft case.
example.fact: Modern forensic fingerprint analysis traces back to Sir Francis Galton's 1892 book classifying fingerprint patterns, building on earlier work by Henry Faulds and William Herschel in colonial India. Scotland Yard adopted fingerprinting for criminal identification in 1901, and it remains one of the oldest biometric techniques still in active use today.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 车来了,大家赶紧上车吧。
example.pinyin: Chē lái le, dàjiā gǎnjǐn shàngchē ba.
example.english: The bus is here, everyone hurry and get on.
example.fact: London's iconic double-decker bus design dates back to horse-drawn omnibuses of the 1850s, when adding an upper deck let operators carry more passengers without lengthening the vehicle or needing more horses. The modern Routemaster model, introduced in 1956, remained in regular service on some routes for over 50 years.

components.note: 冫 pictures ice crystals forming.
水 (water) sits beside it, together showing water turned to ice.
氵 (water) — 淇 names a river; it appears in the name of the Qi River (淇河) in Henan.
其 (qí) gives an exact match for 淇's reading.
氵 (water) — 淋 describes water dripping or drenching something.
林 (lín) gives the sound — an exact match with 淋.

example.hanzi: 夏天最想吃的东西就是冰淇淋。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān zuì xiǎng chī de dōngxi jiù shì bīngqílín.
example.english: In summer, ice cream is what you crave most.
example.fact: Ice cream's ancestor may go back to ancient China, where records describe a chilled dessert made from buffalo milk, flour, and camphor packed into snow around 200 BC. Modern hand-cranked ice cream machines weren't invented until 1843, by American Nancy Johnson, whose design is still the basic mechanism used in home ice cream makers today.

components.note: 用's ancient form has been interpreted as a picture of a wooden bucket or pail, an everyday tool of daily life — objects made for a purpose gave 用 its meaning 'to use, to employ.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

着 developed as a variant of 著, replacing the lower part of that character with 目 (eye) — originally suggesting attention fixed on something, the source of both the aspect-marker sense 'ongoing action' and the meaning 'to touch, to attach.'

example.hanzi: 这么简单的事情用不着请人帮忙。
example.pinyin: Zhème jiǎndān de shìqing yòngbuzháo qǐng rén bāngmáng.
example.english: Such a simple matter doesn't need anyone's help.
example.fact: The principle of minimalism in design, championed by architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe's motto "less is more," argues that unnecessary ornamentation and function that isn't needed should be stripped away entirely. His Barcelona Pavilion of 1929, built almost entirely of glass, steel, and stone with no superfluous decoration, remains a landmark reference for that philosophy.

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'

example.hanzi: 吃了药以后,他感觉好受多了。
example.pinyin: Chīle yào yǐhòu, tā gǎnjué hǎoshòu duō le.
example.english: After taking the medicine, he felt much better.
example.fact: Placebo treatments — pills or procedures with no active medical ingredient — have been shown in clinical trials to measurably reduce pain and reported symptoms in a substantial share of patients, even when those patients are told beforehand that what they're receiving is a placebo. Researchers attribute much of this "open-label placebo" effect to genuine changes in brain chemistry triggered by expectation itself.

components.note: 足 depicts a leg (the upper shape) above a foot — a simple picture of the human leg and foot, giving 足 its meaning 'foot, to be sufficient.'

以's ancient form has been read as a picture of a person bent over, holding or carrying a tool or bundle — the image of using an implement to accomplish a task gave 以 its meaning 'to use, by means of, with.'

example.hanzi: 这些证据足以证明他的清白。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē zhèngjù zúyǐ zhèngmíng tā de qīngbái.
example.english: This evidence is sufficient to prove his innocence.
example.fact: DNA evidence requires only a vanishingly small sample to be conclusive — modern forensic techniques can generate a full genetic profile from as few as five to twenty human cells, far fewer than the number left behind by a single fingerprint touch. This sensitivity is what makes DNA evidence powerful in court, but it also raises the risk of contamination from unrelated, incidental contact.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'

example.hanzi: 他们从大学时代就开始相爱了。
example.pinyin: Tāmen cóng dàxué shídài jiù kāishǐ xiāng'ài le.
example.english: They started loving each other back in their college days.
example.fact: Anthropologist Helen Fisher's brain-imaging studies found that early romantic love activates the same dopamine-rich reward circuits in the brain as cocaine use, which may explain why new relationships can produce an almost addictive intensity of focus on one person. That neural activation pattern tends to ease over time as attachment-related brain regions take over instead.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
贝 (money, from ancient shell currency) — 赖 relates to depending on someone for support, as in 'to rely on.'
剌 (là) gives a sound close to lài, sharing the initial l- and a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的味道真不赖。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de wèidào zhēn bù lài.
example.english: This restaurant's food really isn't bad.
example.fact: Michelin, the tire company, began publishing its restaurant guide in 1900 to encourage French motorists to drive more and wear out their tires faster, only later evolving the guide's star ratings into the internationally respected culinary benchmark they are today. Its anonymous inspectors' identities remain a closely guarded secret even now.

components.note: A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.

example.hanzi: 这座城市的人口已经超过一千万。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de rénkǒu yǐjīng chāoguò yī qiān wàn.
example.english: This city's population has already exceeded ten million.
example.fact: The world's human population passed 8 billion in November 2022, yet demographers project growth will slow sharply and possibly peak later this century, according to United Nations projections, as birth rates fall in more and more countries. Some nations, including Japan and South Korea, are already seeing population decline rather than growth.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'

example.hanzi: 这位年轻画家因为一幅画而出名。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi niánqīng huàjiā yīnwèi yī fú huà ér chūmíng.
example.english: This young painter became famous because of one painting.
example.fact: Vincent van Gogh sold only a single painting during his lifetime and died largely unrecognized in 1890, yet within a few decades his work became some of the most valuable and famous in art history. His sister-in-law Johanna is largely credited with promoting his paintings and letters after his death, building the reputation he never lived to see.
